from.place: proof, proper case: transport of sheaf cohomology through the localized-site equivalence

title: Etale cohomology is invariant under the localized-site sheaf equivalence
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal D$ be Grothendieck sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $e:\mathcal C\simeq\mathcal D$ an equivalence of categories whose forward and inverse functors carry covering families to covering families, inducing an equivalence $e_*$ of categories of abelian sheaves. For an object $W$ of $\mathcal C$, an abelian sheaf $G$ on $\mathcal C$, and every $q\geq0$, the equivalence identifies the derived cohomology over $W$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] with that over $e(W)$: $H^q(W,G)\xrightarrow{\sim}H^q(e(W),e_*G)$. This isomorphism is natural in $G$ and in morphisms of objects $W'\to W$ of $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Cohomology on Sites, Lemma 03F3 (lemma-cohomology-of-open), derived-functor calculation transported by an equivalence of sites (agent extension)

proof.text: Let $e':\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ be the inverse functor, with natural isomorphisms $\eta:\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}\cong e'\circ e$ and $\varepsilon:e\circ e'\cong\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal D}$. First, a family $\{f_a:X_a\to X\}_{a\in A}$ of $\mathcal C$ is a covering iff $\{e(f_a)\}_{a\in A}$ is a covering of $\mathcal D$: 'only if' is the hypothesis on $e$; if $\{e(f_a)\}$ is a covering, so is $\{e'e(f_a)\}$ by the hypothesis on $e'$, and $e'e(f_a)\circ\eta_{X_a}=\eta_X\circ f_a$ with $\eta_{X_a},\eta_X$ isomorphisms, so $\{f_a\}$ is a covering by [lem-weil-pbc-site-covering-isomorphic-family] (with $g_a=e'e(f_a)$, $\sigma_a=\eta_{X_a}$, $\varphi=\eta_X$, and the reindexing convention of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1)). Hence [lem-weil-pbc-site-equivalence-is-morphism-of-sites](3), applied to $p=e$, $p'=e'$, shows that $e_*:=e'^s$, $G\mapsto G\circ e'$, is an equivalence $\textit{Ab}(\mathcal C)\to\textit{Ab}(\mathcal D)$ with quasi-inverse $e^s$; it is additive since sums of morphisms of abelian sheaves are computed sectionwise. For every abelian sheaf $G$ on $\mathcal C$ and object $W$ of $\mathcal C$, $(e_*G)(e(W))=G(e'e(W))$, and $G(\eta_W):G(e'e(W))\to G(W)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $G$ and in $W$ by naturality of $\eta$.

source.place: Sites, Lemma Tag 03A0 (lemma-equivalence), specialized to an equivalence of sites carrying coverings to coverings in both directions

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $s:G\to I^\bullet$ in $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal C)$. The additive equivalence $e_*$ carries it to an injective resolution $e_*G\to e_*I^\bullet$ in $\operatorname{Ab}(\mathcal D)$, since it carries injectives to injectives and exact sequences to exact sequences; it also carries morphisms of resolutions and their homotopies.

source.place: Homology, Lemma Tag 015Z (lemma-adjoint-preserve-injectives), as used in Cohomology on Sites, Lemma Tag 03YU

proof.text: Evaluation on the corresponding objects gives an isomorphism of cochain complexes $\Gamma(e(W),e_*I^\bullet)=I^\bullet(e'e(W))\xrightarrow{I^\bullet(\eta_W)}I^\bullet(W)=\Gamma(W,I^\bullet)$ (a map of complexes since the differentials are morphisms of sheaves, step 1), and it is compatible with the augmentation and with morphisms $W'\to W$. By the definition of cohomology over an object as the cohomology of sections of an injective resolution, taking cohomology yields natural isomorphisms $H^q(W,G)\cong H^q(e(W),e_*G)$ for every $q\ge0$; the degree-zero map is the canonical identification of sections.
